question_text: What is the function of DNA polymerase?

insider_note: Two properties: it is fast and it is accurate. Both are worth stating, because the accuracy is what makes replication reliable.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Its function
steps.margin_note: Name the reaction, the process, and the direction.
lines: DNA POLYMERASE catalyses the polymerisation of
deoxyribonucleotides into a new DNA strand,
It adds nucleotides only in the 5' to 3'
steps.why: The enzyme can only add to a free 3' end, which is why replication runs in one direction along each strand.
common_mistakes: Saying it makes RNA. That is RNA polymerase.
Saying it works in both directions. It adds only 5' to 3'.
steps.memory_tip: It builds DNA, and only one way along it.

steps.label: Speed and accuracy
steps.margin_note: Both properties named, then one line on why both matter.
lines: It polymerises a very large number of nucleotides
It works with a HIGH DEGREE OF ACCURACY: about
one error in a billion base pairs.
Both properties are needed, because an inaccurate
copy would be a mutation in every generation.
steps.why: A genome copied quickly but carelessly would accumulate mutations faster than selection could remove them, so speed alone is not enough.
common_mistakes: Giving only the speed. The ACCURACY is the second half of the mark.
Saying it never makes errors. It makes very few, not none.
steps.memory_tip: Speed without accuracy would be useless.
